subject: tu:game/game/gamemain
value: THE gGameMode RESPELLING CAMPAIGN IS COMPLETE except for one deliberately excluded TU. v1 listed 135 raw-literal sites across 16 TUs; waves 1-2 cleared gamemain.c, screensaver.c, world/camera.c, ui/options.c and world/items.c, and wave 3 (attempt.gamemode-conversion-wave3.20260831.v1) cleared all 13 remaining TUs in 63 sites: player.c 59, gauntworld.c 5, message.c 5, pmotion.c 4, auxscreen.c 4, bosscam.c 3, select.c 3, sounds.c 2, and one each in enemy.c, combat.c, shop.c, newcam.c, tower.c. Every one was byte-identical under defake_gate, with full ninja green and project progress unchanged at 98.06% fuzzy / 61.27% matched. A project-wide sweep now finds NO remaining `gGameMode <cmp> literal`, case arm, or assignment anywhere in src/. STILL OPEN: only game/audio/sndfx.c, held out because another lane owned it during wave 3 -- and it should NOT simply be converted, because v1's semantic anomaly (a) is unresolved and is a symbol-identity question, not a spelling one: sndFxInit assigns a POINTER into `gGameMode` (sndfx.c:217, `gGameMode = (s32)a;` where `a` is a void* parameter) while the same file's sndFxPaused() macro reads it as a mode via `gGameMode & 0x8000`. Those two uses cannot both be the real gGameMode; settle the identity before respelling anything there. DELIBERATELY LEFT RAW EVERYWHERE, and this is now the campaign's settled position rather than an omission: the `gGameMode & 0x8000` / `& 0x4000` FAMILY-BIT tests (player.c x4, gauntworld.c x4, gamemain.c x6, message.c, combat.c, items.c, screensaver.c, camera.c). These classify a mode's family instead of comparing against one mode, so no single enum constant is a truthful spelling -- MA_CREDITS happens to equal 0x8000, and substituting it would assert a false identity. gamemode.h's own header comment documents this group idiom. CORRECTIONS TO v1's THREE CORRECTIONS, from the wave-3 sweep: (i) v1 said player.c's debt is mostly in `switch (gGameMode)` CASE ARMS and that 'player.c:775 has more' arms than camera.c's 15 -- that is wrong in both directions. player.c's switch is a ONE-CASE switch (`case 0x4010: break; default: return;`), contributing exactly 1 arm; player.c's debt is almost entirely `==`/`!=` comparisons, 58 of its 59 sites. The 'scan switch bodies or under-count by half' warning was real for camera.c but does not generalize. (ii) v1's per-TU counts were otherwise accurate, but its site model missed two literal FORMS that a `==`-and-case scan cannot see: plain ASSIGNMENTS (`gGameMode = 0x400B` in select.c:2806, shop.c:1340, and DECIMAL ones in auxscreen.c:755/1157 spelled 16398/16399), and arithmetic RANGE TESTS (`(u32)(gGameMode - 0x400F) <= 1` at player.c:1004). Both convert byte-identically; a future respelling sweep of any enum must cover compare, case, assignment, and arithmetic operand positions in every base. (iii) v1 flagged items.c's `extern u32 gGameMode` divergence (fixed in wave 2); the same class of divergence also exists as `extern int gGameMode` in message.c and screensaver.c, where every other TU uses s32. Since types.h defines s32 as `signed long`, not `int`, these are genuine declaration divergences rather than spelling noise. message.c was harmonized to s32 in wave 3 (byte-identical); screensaver.c:117 was outside wave 3's scope and REMAINS DIVERGENT for a future owner. Also corrected in wave 3: enemy.c's extern comment described gGameMode as 'current map/world id', which is simply false -- its only site tests MA_HSTABLE, an attract-loop mode.
